title: Indie hackers build AI factories but have no money or traffic: distribution is the gap
summary: Levels shares a friend's report from an indie hacker meetup: builders obsess over code-generating systems and agent pipelines while lacking customers, revenue, and any idea where to get traffic. The post frames AI-era building as a comfortable way to avoid marketing and distribution.

principles.text: Building elaborate dev tooling is a comfortable substitute for the harder work of finding traffic and money.
principles.quote: almost everyone is super focused on development.

principles.text: Optimizing your build system produces no business if you have no traffic or revenue and don't know how to get either.
principles.quote: but the most interesting part is that almost none of them have money or traffic.

principles.text: Don't postpone marketing until your system is perfect; 'finish the system first, then market' is a trap.
principles.quote: yeah, i should probably do on marketing, but first i’ll finish my super system and then i’ll start.

principles.text: AI makes the old trap of building in a basement without showing anyone worse, flooding the world with unneeded products.
principles.quote: now it’s even worse: the amount of useless aislop nobody needs has grown massively.
